paragraphs.title: Job: His Character, Family, and Wealth

answers: Perfect, upright, God-fearing, and one who eschewed evil
Poor, angry, and without a family
A king who ruled over Uz
easy.explanation: Job is described as perfect and upright, fearing God and eschewing evil.
easy.q: How is Job described at the beginning of the chapter?

answers: Six sons and four daughters
Seven sons and three daughters
Three sons and seven daughters
easy.explanation: Job had seven sons and three daughters.
easy.q: How many sons and daughters did Job have?

answers: They went to war
They worked only in the fields
They feasted in their houses, every one his day
easy.explanation: Job's sons went and feasted in their houses, each on his appointed day.

answers: He feared that they might have sinned in their hearts
He wanted to increase his wealth
His children demanded the offerings
medium.explanation: Job said, “It may be that my sons have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts.”
medium.q: Why did Job offer burnt offerings for his children?

answers: He owned only a few sheep
He had thousands of sheep and camels and hundreds of oxen and she asses
He owned many houses in Jerusalem
medium.explanation: Job had seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred she asses.
medium.q: Which detail shows Job's great wealth?

answers: Five hundred sheep
Five hundred camels
Five hundred pairs of oxen
medium.explanation: A yoke refers to a pair, so five hundred yoke means five hundred pairs of oxen.
medium.q: What does “five hundred yoke of oxen” mean?

answers: He regularly cared for the spiritual condition of his children
He offered only after one of them certainly sinned
He stopped caring for them after their feasts
challenge.explanation: The word “continually” shows that Job's concern and offerings were ongoing.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Job offering burnt offerings continually?

answers: His wealth is described as unimportant
He was the greatest of all the men of the east
He was the least important man in the region
challenge.explanation: The passage says that Job was “the greatest of all the men of the east.”
challenge.q: How is Job's wealth connected with his position among other people?

answers: The feasts caused Job to join them every time
The feasts made Job angry with his children
After the feasts, Job sanctified them and offered burnt offerings for them
challenge.explanation: After their feasting days, Job sanctified his children and offered offerings because they might have sinned.
challenge.q: What was the connection between the children's feasts and Job's actions?

paragraphs.title: The Heavenly Assembly and the Debate over Job's Faith

answers: The sons of God, and Satan also among them
Job's children only
The kings of the land of Uz
easy.explanation: The sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan came among them.
easy.q: Who appeared before the LORD in the heavenly assembly?

answers: He had come from Job's house
He had been going to and fro in the earth and walking up and down in it
He had come only from the wilderness
easy.explanation: Satan answered that he had been going to and fro in the earth and walking up and down in it.
easy.q: What did Satan say when the LORD asked where he had come from?

answers: Job himself
The sons of God
All that Job had, but not Job himself
easy.explanation: The LORD placed all that Job had in Satan's power but commanded him not to put forth his hand against Job himself.
easy.q: What did the LORD allow Satan to attack?

answers: Job feared God because he had received protection and prosperity
Job did not know God
Job feared only for the sake of his children
medium.explanation: Satan pointed to the hedge around Job, his house, and his possessions, as well as the blessing upon his work.
medium.q: What did Satan claim was the reason for Job's fear of God?

answers: As wealthy but not upright
As perfect, upright, God-fearing, and one who eschewed evil
As careless about his conduct
medium.explanation: The LORD repeated that Job was perfect and upright, feared God, and eschewed evil.
medium.q: How did the LORD describe Job in His answer to Satan?

answers: You have abandoned him
You have tested him
You have protected and surrounded him
medium.explanation: Satan said that the LORD had placed a protective hedge around Job, his house, and all that he had.
medium.q: What does “Hast thou made an hedge about him” mean in context?

answers: Whether Job's children were wealthier than he was
Whether Job's fear of God was genuine or depended on blessing and protection
Whether Job lived in the land of Uz
challenge.explanation: Satan argued that Job served God because of his favorable circumstances, while Job's faith was being tested.
challenge.q: What is the central issue in the debate between the LORD and Satan concerning Job?

answers: Satan could attack Job's possessions but not Job himself
Satan could attack Job but not his possessions
Satan could attack neither Job nor his possessions
challenge.explanation: The LORD said, “all that he hath is in thy power,” but commanded Satan not to put forth his hand upon Job himself.
challenge.q: What limit was placed on the first test of Job?

answers: It proved that Satan did not know Job
It explained why Job had left his family
Satan used the protection and blessing as evidence that Job's fear of God depended on them
challenge.explanation: Satan claimed that Job would turn against God if his protection and prosperity were removed.
challenge.q: Why was the hedge around Job important to Satan's argument?

paragraphs.title: Disasters Strike Job's Possessions and Children

answers: They were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house
They were working in the fields
They were traveling through the wilderness
easy.explanation: They were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house.
easy.q: What were Job's sons and daughters doing when the disasters began?

answers: They were sold
The fire of God fell from heaven and consumed them
They escaped into another land
easy.explanation: The fire of God fell from heaven, burned up the sheep and servants, and consumed them.
easy.q: What happened to the sheep and servants?

answers: They moved to another house
They escaped from the storm
They died when the house fell upon them
easy.explanation: A great wind struck the house, causing it to fall upon the young people, who died.
easy.q: What happened to Job's sons and daughters?

answers: Oxen and asses, sheep, camels, and finally Job's sons and daughters
Job's children, camels, sheep, and finally oxen and asses
Sheep, Job's children, oxen and asses, and finally camels
medium.explanation: The messengers first reported the oxen and asses, then the sheep, then the camels, and finally the children.
medium.q: In what order did the reports of disaster arrive?

answers: The fire from heaven
The Chaldeans
The great wind from the wilderness
medium.explanation: The Chaldeans formed three bands, attacked the camels, and carried them away.
medium.q: Who caused the loss of the camels?

answers: The messenger was the only person sent
The messenger hid the report
The messenger alone survived in order to bring Job the news
medium.explanation: Each messenger said that he alone had escaped so that he could tell Job what had happened.
medium.q: What does “I only am escaped alone to tell thee” mean?

answers: The reports arrived one after another while the previous messenger was still speaking
All the messengers arrived together after many days
Job discovered each disaster by himself
challenge.explanation: The repeated phrase “While he was yet speaking” emphasizes the rapid succession of calamities.
challenge.q: What intensifies the description of the disasters?

answers: The possessions were lost only in the house, while the children were lost only in the fields
The possessions were taken or destroyed by raids and fire, while the children died when the house collapsed
The possessions and children were all lost in exactly the same way

challenge.q: What distinction is made between the disasters affecting the possessions and those affecting the children?

answers: It was the place where they had gathered for their feast
Job had commanded them to remain there
They were not actually in a house when the disaster occurred
challenge.explanation: All the children were gathered in the eldest brother's house, which the great wind struck and caused to fall.
challenge.q: Why is it significant that the children were in their eldest brother's house?

paragraphs.title: Job's Mourning and His Stand before God

answers: He left the land
He rent his mantle and shaved his head
He called for another feast

easy.q: What did Job do after hearing the reports?

The LORD gave nothing
The LORD took only his possessions
easy.explanation: Job said, “The LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD.”
easy.q: What did Job say about the LORD?

answers: Yes, he sinned many times
The passage says nothing about it
No, he did not sin or charge God foolishly
easy.explanation: The chapter concludes, “In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly.”
easy.q: Did Job sin after the disasters?

answers: Joy over his success
Deep mourning
Preparation for a journey
medium.explanation: These actions were customary expressions of grief and mourning.
medium.q: What do the rending of Job's mantle and the shaving of his head express?

answers: He fell down upon the ground and worshipped
He went to fight the Chaldeans
He searched for his children

medium.q: What did Job do after rending his mantle and shaving his head?

answers: Gave God a gift
Prayed to God
Blamed or spoke against God in a foolish way
medium.explanation: The phrase means that Job did not foolishly accuse or condemn God because of his losses.
medium.q: In the context of Job 1:22, what does “charged God foolishly” mean?

answers: He mourns, yet worships and acknowledges that the LORD gives and takes away
He hides his grief and denies the disasters
He becomes angry and refuses to worship

challenge.q: How does Job combine mourning and faith?

answers: He plans to leave the land immediately
He recognizes that he brought nothing into the world and will take no possessions out of it
He lost only his clothing
challenge.explanation: Job recognizes the temporary nature of earthly possessions and human life.
challenge.q: What does Job mean by “Naked came I out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return thither”?

answers: He lost everything but remained faithful and did not sin

He rejoiced over the disasters despite losing everything
challenge.explanation: Although Job suffered devastating losses, the passage says that he did not sin or charge God foolishly.
